<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours of one tiny island. Almost nothing happens, on purpose.</b><br>
  A stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube: one young woman, one tall palm, one raft and a lot of time. She idles, nodding to the music on her headphones. Every so often something happens: a bottle washes straight back, a drone delivers a spare pair of headphones, a coconut lands on a hermit crab and the crab walks off wearing it. Each gag starts on the next bar of the music, so it lands on the beat.
</p>

<p align="center">
  <sub>An unofficial remake, inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, and not affiliated with it or its owners. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime. 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, and always daytime. Every sound is synthesized from code.</sub>
</p>

```sh
# live preview, and export to MP4
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<details>
<summary><b>GREETINGS</b>: who is who on the island</summary>

<br>

| Greeted | Why |
| --- | --- |
| The sea turtle | Visits. Keeps a calm head about it. |
| The grey tabby on the crate | Arrives on a crate, climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats away again. Comes back another time. |
| The shark in headphones | Nods to the beat. Has taste. |
| The hermit crab | A coconut falls on it, and then the coconut walks off with the crab wearing it. |
| The delivery drone | Brings a parcel. The parcel is another pair of headphones. |
| The bro on the electric hydrofoil | Waves with a shaka and carves off. |
| The tour boat | Full of selfie-takers. |
| The kumara | She plants it, and it grows over the course of the video. |
| The bottle | A message in a bottle washes straight back. Later a different bottle brings a reply. |
| ~~The ship~~ | Sails past exactly while she is busy. Even waits for her to get busy. No greeting. |

Between visitors she keeps herself busy: coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, a sandcastle that the tide takes, waving for rescue, the signal hunt (one bar of signal, at the top of the palm), and bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing. She could leave any time: she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE SCHEDULE</b>: four timers and a great deal of calm</summary>

<br>

[activities.toml](activities.toml) listed 94 activities on 2026-10-01 (81 on four timers, 13 chained follow-ups that only start when another activity calls them), and it grows every few hours. In a typical 10-hour run (the median of 200 simulated runs):

| Timer | Comes round every | Events in a 10-hour run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular | 2 to 5 minutes | about 155 |
| Occasional | 12 to 25 minutes | about 30 |
| Rare | 30 to 60 minutes | about 13 |
| Super rare | 3 to 6 hours (at most 3 a run) | about 2 |

Plus chained follow-ups, such as the tide that comes for each sandcastle. She is busy about a third of the time and idles the rest. Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut. Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992.

The scene has a life of its own too: 26 entries, 4 always-on effects and 22 timed events. Shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

```sh
python tools/schedule.py           # validate, then simulate a 10-hour run
python tools/render_demo.py --dev  # dev reel of every activity, with a HUD
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE SOUND</b>: synthesized, every last gull</summary>

<br>

- Everything is synthesized from code in [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, borrowed loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far.
- The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (a ii-V-I-vi progression): 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The ocean ambience is a seamless 60-second loop as well.
- The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP. Levels are adjustable in master and per routine.
- Nobody has listened to any of it yet. The intro above is silent, which is at least accurate.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE MACHINE</b>: what actually runs it</summary>

<br>

```text
 RENDERER ...... WEB/INDEX.HTML, PLAIN ES MODULES, NO BUILD STEP
 SERVER ........ TOOLS/SERVE.PY ON 127.0.0.1:8765
 VIDEO ......... WEBCODECS H.264 IN THE BROWSER, FRAME-EXACT
 SPEED ......... 68 TO 78 FRAMES A SECOND AT 1080P30 IN CHROME
 SOUND ......... MIXED BY THE SERVER, JOINED INTO ONE MP4
 NPM PACKAGES .. NONE
 MOTION ........ HARD CUTS AND STEPPED MOVEMENT
 PLOT .......... MINIMAL
```

The web page is the renderer: live preview, and export to a YouTube-ready MP4. `python tools/render_demo.py --dev` is the older Python reference renderer, kept for its dev reel.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>ABOUT THIS INTRO</b>: how the banner is made</summary>

<br>

The banner copies the layout of a mid-1980s Commodore 64 one-screen intro, the kind that ran before the main program: a big logo on black, a fenced PRESENTS, one line on a pink raster bar and one on a blue one, a dated "... ON dd/mm/yy BY ..." line, a small info block, a blinking PRESS SPACE and one scroller. Here the date line says who stranded her (the random seed), and the info block lists the plot.

- **Logo.** A character mosaic: each letter is 4 or 5 cells wide and 6 high, every cell full, empty, a half block or a 45-degree wedge. It clips a stack of one-scanline stripes (a sea ramp, then a sand ramp) that rolls up 16 lines a second, which is the raster split, rolling.
- **Colours.** Only the 16 VIC-II colours, at Pepto's measured values. Bar shading and fades run in luminance order.
- **Type.** An 8x8 font drawn for this banner; the scroller is the same font at 2x2, shaded per scanline.
- **Sprites.** Two 24x21 sprites, expanded to double size. A real C64 would need more sprites than it owns to colour them like this, so consider them aspirational.
- **Motion.** Everything but the scroller keeps time with the theme at 80 BPM: the sprites nod and PRESS SPACE blinks on the beat, a glint runs down each bar once a beat, the colour wash goes round once a beat and the logo stripes come round every two. No colour cycle brings white back to the same spot more than 1.4 times a second, well under the 3 Hz flash limit, and with reduced motion switched on everything holds on a complete first frame.

No group's logo, character set, picture or scrolltext was copied; every letter, sprite and word is new, and the whole banner is rebuilt by one small Node script with no dependencies.

</details>
